body.text: The FHP gives a water-based environment for intermediate-term storage of spent fuel and stores non-fuel irradiated core assemblies before disposal.

body.text: It provides core assembly cooling, spent fuel reactivity control, fission product containment, and radiation shielding.
body.anchor: The FHP provides core assembly cooling, spent fuel reactivity control

body.text: The SFP is sized for ten years of spent fuel from normal operation plus other core assemblies.

body.text: The fuel storage area holds seven intact fuel racks and one failed fuel rack.

body.text: The stainless steel liner has a leak chase system. There are no pool wall penetrations below the elevation of stored core assemblies.

body.text: The SFP does not use soluble boron. Racks hold fuel subcritical by geometry control and fixed borated neutron absorbers.

body.text: The BLTC transfers core assemblies into the PIC, where a cleaning vessel gives a controlled environment to chemically clean and remove residual sodium.
body.anchor: provides a controlled environment within the PIC to chemically clean and remove residual sodium coolant

body.text: The cleaning vessel isolates assemblies from the surroundings to prevent sodium-water interactions.
body.anchor: isolates core assemblies from the surrounding environment to prevent sodium-water interactions

body.text: During cleaning, heat passes through the cleaning vessel to the SFP water.
body.anchor: heat is passively transferred through the cleaning vessel to the SFP water

body.text: Gaseous effluent is filtered and sent to the FHB portion of the NI HVAC. Liquid effluent goes to the FPP.
body.anchor: while liquid effluent is transferred to the FPP

body.text: After cleaning and rinsing, the PIC elevator lowers the assembly, and a horizontal trolley moves it upright to the cask loading pit.
body.anchor: the PIC uses a horizontal trolley to transfer the core assembly upright to the cask loading pit area

body.text: A fuel assembly with indicated cladding damage is sealed in an FFC inerted with helium.
body.anchor: encapsulate a fuel assembly with indicated fuel pin cladding damage inside an FFC

body.text: No sodium cleaning occurs. The failed assembly goes directly into the FFC from the BLTC.
body.anchor: No sodium cleaning occurs for a failed fuel assembly

body.text: The FFC prevents metallic uranium-water interactions and sodium-water reactions that can occur due to cladding failure in sodium-bonded fuel.
body.anchor: prevent metallic uranium-water interactions and sodium-water reactions

body.text: Closure welds are done after the canister is voided and back-filled, while the FFC is in the PIC basket.

body.text: The FPC is NST. It has two independent trains that send heat to the NI Water System.
body.anchor: The FPC consists of two independent cooling trains

body.text: Each train is sized for the entire SFP heat load.
body.anchor: Each train is sized to remove the entire heat load of the SFP

body.text: The FPP is a single purification train with anion and cation exchange resins.
body.anchor: The FPP consists of a single purification train

body.text: FPC and FPP suction and discharge lines are located to prevent draining the SFP below a minimum safe level.
body.anchor: The suction and discharge lines of the FPC are located to prevent draining

o: Location of the suction and discharge lines

body.text: If normal cooling is unavailable, core assemblies are cooled passively by natural circulation in the SFP.
body.anchor: then core assemblies are passively cooled by natural circulation within the SFP

body.text: If active cooling is lost, the SFP relies on evaporation and redundant makeup systems.
body.anchor: the SFP relies on evaporation to passively cool spent fuel assemblies

body.text: The water volume cools spent fuel for at least 7 days without makeup at a full SFP heat load.
body.anchor: The water volume of the SFP cools spent fuel for at least 7 days without makeup

body.text: Normal makeup comes from the NI Water System. Emergency makeup comes from offsite sources through an external fill leg.
body.anchor: Makeup water is provided from a connection to NI Water System during normal operations

body.text: No powered SSCs are needed for emergency makeup through the fill leg.
body.anchor: No powered SSCs are required to provide emergency makeup water via the exterior fill leg

body.text: SFP level sensors start refill on low level during normal operation and also support PAM.

checks.anchor: No powered SSCs are required to provide emergency makeup water via the exterior fill leg

title: Water Pool Fuel Handling System
subject: FHP
intro: The FHP is where spent fuel ends up. It takes assemblies out of sodium, cleans them, and stores them under water with passive cooling as the safety function.
